newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-SIIMAN SEEKS PARLIAMENT APPROVAL TO BE PM.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-SIIMAN SEEKS PARLIAMENT APPROVAL TO BE PM.

text.p: Estonia's nominated prime minister, Mart Siiman, will go before parliament on Wednesday to seek approval from the house, a spokeswoman for the parliament said.
Spokeswoman Margit Liivoja said Siiman, 50, would make a speech to the parliament at 1400 (1200 GMT) and then the house's 101 members could each ask him up to two questions.
Parliament will then vote whether to accept him as the new prime minister to replace Tiit Vaehi who stepped down last month.
"When he is approved he has seven days to put together a government with 15 ministers, including himself, then he will come back to parliament again for approval," Liivoja told Reuters.
"If the government is approved, then the president (Lennart Meri) has three days to appoint him as prime minister."
Siiman, a leading minority government politician, currently heads the parliamentary faction of the Coalition Party, the biggest grouping in parliament.
He is taking over from Vaehi, a veteran Coalition Party politician who has been in office since April 1995.
Vaehi stepped down last month after only narrowly winning a parliament no-confidence vote amid allegations that he took part in shady privatisation deals.
Estonia is currently ruled by a minority administration of the Coalition Party and a block of rural parties which commands the support of 41 seats in the 101 seat house.
Siiman was a television and radio manager from the pre-Soviet and post-Soviet era.
Political analysts and financial market players were not expecting any changes to current policies under a Siiman-led government.
